# THE BOUNDARY MANIFEST — every tracked JavaScript/TypeScript file, and what it is.
#
# One rule per line:  CLASS | pattern | reason | producer
#
#   CLASS     LOGIC (must become Rust, counted and capped) · BOUNDARY (a platform call, decides nothing)
#             · RENDERING (places what it was given) · GENERATED (a build step produces it)
#   pattern   repo-relative. A trailing `/` matches the whole tree; anything else is one exact file.
#             THE MOST SPECIFIC (LONGEST) MATCHING PATTERN WINS, so the order of these lines never decides.
#   reason    what it is, in one line — the thing a reviewer checks
#   producer  REQUIRED for GENERATED: the path of the thing that produces the file, checked to exist
#
# The gate is agent/tests/js_boundary_inventory.rs. LOGIC is the work that is left; its cap only falls.
#
# ── TWO RULES THAT MAKE THE HARD CASES A RULE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT CALL ────────────────────────────────────
#
# A TEST BELONGS TO THE CODE IT TESTS. That is why `gateway/test/` is LOGIC — those files exercise the console
# worker's TypeScript and leave when it does — and why `agent/scripts/e2e/` is BOUNDARY: that suite drives the
# DEVICE's HTTP surface, whose subject is already Rust, so it is a harness rather than work that is left. A test
# whose subject is Rust is not a migration item; a test whose subject is JavaScript goes with its subject.
#
# **AND A TEST FILE IS TWO THINGS, WHICH THIS RULE WAS READ AS ONE.** The e2e suite was cleared as BOUNDARY on
# the sentence above, and the sentence was true of half of it: the DRIVING is a harness. The other half was 74
# `check(...)` call sites that computed their conditions, derived the details a reader acts on, and decided
# whether a device passed — the ASSERTIONS, which are this manifest's LOGIC definition verbatim and which the
# rule above says nothing about. Read by its control flow rather than its name (which is the standard the audit
# of 2026-10-08 set and did not apply here), the assertion half moved to `agent/e2e-judge/`, and the rule is
# now true of the whole file rather than of its subject. **A test's SETUP is a boundary; a test's VERDICT is
# not** — and the same reading applies to the sweeps' payloads, which is why their probe snippets stay JS and
# their judge does not.
#
# A FIXTURE IS NOT A DECISION. `panel-stub.cjs` answers thirty comparisons and every one of them decides what the
# FAKE device returns — test data, not product behaviour. The same reading covers a probe SOURCE (it ships as text
# into a page), an assembler (a build step), and a harness renderer (it builds the surface under test). What makes
# a file LOGIC is that something the PRODUCT does depends on it.

# ── BOUNDARY: a platform call, and it decides nothing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/src/lib/ | the panel's data boundary — fetch, storage, DOM reads, and the seams that call the logic crate
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/src/hooks/ | the panel's SSE/fetch hooks — a transport, not a decision
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/src/wasm/panelLogic.ts | the hand-written seam onto the panel's logic crate
BOUNDARY | agent/resources/panel-react/scripts/ | the panel's CSS build tooling
BOUNDARY | gateway/ui/src/wasm/consoleLogic.ts | the hand-written seam onto the console's logic crate
BOUNDARY | gateway/ui/scripts/ | the console's build tooling
BOUNDARY | gateway/scripts/ | the console worker's build/deploy tooling
BOUNDARY | gateway/wasm/ | harnesses that execute the built JS+wasm worker and diff it against the shipping one
BOUNDARY | index/worker/ | the same harness shape for the index worker
BOUNDARY | index/landing/ | harnesses that render and verify the landing crate's output
BOUNDARY | index/spike-rust-landing/ | the landing spike's measure/verify harness
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-workspace-dsh/ | the DSH plugin package — a plugin must be JS; the agent owns the connections
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-cli/parity/ | the CLI's decision corpus and the instrument that checks it. It WAS a differential (the TypeScript's answers against the Rust's, `ts.mjs` against `summrise-cli-parity`); the cutover deleted the TypeScript, so the answers were FROZEN into `expected.json` FIRST — 162 cases, captured while both implementations existed and agreed 0 differing — and `compare.mjs` now diffs the Rust against that file. It decides nothing about the product: it spawns a binary and compares strings
BOUNDARY | agent/sweep-plan/parity/ | the parity instrument — it runs the PRE-CHANGE emitter, executes the payload it prints against a stub browser, and diffs that trace against the Rust plan; it decides nothing about the product
# ── AND THE THREE TOOLS ARE BOUNDARY, WHICH THE DIRECTORY RULE COULD NOT SEE (2026-10-09) ────────────────────
# `agent/scripts/` is LOGIC as a rule, and the audit of the sweeps named what stays inside it: the judge's
# JavaScript twin, the two payloads that drive and decide, the two small checkers, and the e2e suite — whose
# DRIVER is what stays now: its plan and its judge left for `agent/e2e-judge/` on 2026-10-10. The three
# TOOLS were never in that list, and reading them line by line says why: each one dispatches on argv, FORWARDS
# `--passes` to the Rust plan without interpreting it, holds path constants and (for the landing) the fixture's
# URLs and page list, and assembles the emitted bundle through `lib/sweep-bundle.mjs`. The decisions they look
# like they make are all somewhere else — which plan runs (Rust), which passes it wants (Rust), what the verdict
# is (Rust). What they do is emit and dispatch, so they are the boundary the rest of this block is.
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/design-sweep.mjs | the shared collector and driver: the four probes as SOURCE STRINGS a browser evaluates, the passes that drive and measure, and the URL/escape helpers. It no longer formats anything — the acknowledgement notes moved to the judge (2026-10-09), which prints them before every exit — and as of landing 2 (2026-10-10) **EVERY DECISION THOSE PASSES CONSULT IS RUST**: `pressDelta`/`loudnessOf`/`DECORATIVE_WAIVERS` are `summrise-sweep-judge`'s `press`/`loudness`/`waivers` (compared against these very functions by a differential and by `sweep-judge/tests/waivers.rs`), the run ORDER and the CAPS the passes spend are the judge's `plan.rs` (`LADDER`, `budgets`) reaching the payload as data through `summrise-design-sweep-driver --emit`, and the Playwright calls that remain — `page.mouse.down`, `page.evaluate`, `page.emulateMedia` — are platform calls that decide nothing. **THE PROBES STAY FOR THE REASON THAT CANNOT BE ARGUED AWAY: `browser_run_script` TAKES A JS FILE.** They are read out of this file at emit time by `summrise-design-sweep-driver` and embedded unchanged (no transcription), and the assembled program is `node --check`ed before it ships, because a probe that stopped parsing returns zero rows — which reads as a clean sweep
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/panel-design-sweep.mjs | the panel tool: argv dispatch, the in-page MOTION/TIMING probe SNIPPETS (strings a browser evaluates), the harness content stamp, and the emit through lib/sweep-bundle.mjs. It interprets no flag and decides no verdict
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/console-design-sweep.mjs | the console tool, the same shape: dispatch, `--passes` forwarded verbatim to the Rust plan, the entry stamp, the emit
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/landing-design-sweep.mjs | the landing tool: it RENDERS the surface under test (the fixture's URLs and page list) and emits it. Fixture data, not product behaviour
# AND THE SAME SPECIES, ONE LANDING LATER (landing 6): the policy's CASES are Rust now (summrise-url-policy
# src/tests.rs, 11 of them, ported case for case from the deleted test/url-policy.test.mjs), and what this
# file does is LOAD the committed wasm artifact in Node and call it — the one thing the Rust cases cannot
# do, because the shell's main process imports electron and no suite here can start it. It pins the
# exported surface, the boundary coercions a wasm `&str` parameter gets wrong, and the refusal shape; a
# harness that executes an artifact, exactly as gateway/wasm/verify.mjs is.
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/test/url-policy-wasm.test.mjs | it requires the built glue and executes the committed .wasm in Node; it decides nothing (the cases are Rust)
# THE SAME SPECIES, ONE LANDING LATER (6b), WITH ONE ASSERTION THE FIRST ONE HAS NO NEED FOR: the 57
# exports of `summrise_shell_policy.js` must NOT include the url policy's 18 names. wasm-bindgen exports
# the whole crate GRAPH, so a dependency between the two crates would make each glue compile its OWN
# `.wasm` and url-policy's `thread_local!` port state would exist twice — `setAgentPort(7740)` through one
# module leaving the other at 18080, which is a custom-port install where the DSH door admits the wrong
# origin. That is not a boundary question; it is the shape of the artifact, and this is the only place it
# can be seen. Everything else here is the first file's job: load the committed bytes, call every export,
# pin the coercions.
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/test/shell-policy-wasm.test.mjs | it requires the built glue and executes the committed .wasm in Node; it decides nothing (the cases are Rust)
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep-plan.mjs | the EMIT-TIME half of the plan: it runs `summrise-sweep-plan` and parses its stdout — one process call, no decision. The plan itself is Rust (agent/sweep-plan/)
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/plan-runtime.cjs | the PAYLOAD-side half: it turns a surface's fields into `page.setViewportSize` / `goto` / `emulateMedia` / `reload` and answers `wants(name)` from the plan's own map — platform calls, and it decides nothing (every boolean it reads is serialized by the Rust rather than defaulted here)
BOUNDARY | agent/src/plugins/playwright/helper.js | the page-side helper the playwright plugin drives
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/e2e/ | **THE DRIVER — AND THIS RULE WAS `LOGIC` FOR A DAY, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** It was classified BOUNDARY by its NAME, reclassified LOGIC on 2026-10-10 by reading its CONTROL FLOW (the standard the manifest's own comment above sets, and the reading this rule had not been given), and is BOUNDARY again because the thing that made it LOGIC has LEFT THE FILE: its `check(...)` call sites — which COMPUTED their conditions (`.some(...)`, `rs === 'OK'`, `text.includes('E2E-SESSION-OK')`, `state === 'partial'`) and DERIVED the sentences a reader triages a failure from — are `agent/e2e-judge/` now, with the section ladder that chose what ran and the policy caps and floors. That is the cut the design sweeps made, their in-page COLLECTOR staying JS while the JUDGE and the PLAN became Rust. **AND THE RECLASSIFICATION WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE CLASS WHILE OFF BY ONE ON THE COUNT**: it says 75 calls, and the file carries **74 call sites** — the 75th `check(` in it is the function's own DEFINITION and the 76th is that comment; a clean run registers 76 checks, because the six `mcp` ones run once per transport and four sites are alternative arms a green run does not take. **The port found that, which is what a count is for.** What is left here performs the platform calls — `fetch` against the agent's own tool surface, a CDP WebSocket to 9333, the `browser_run_script` payload STRINGS a browser evaluates, `require('node:fs')` for its own scratch files, and the polling loops that wait for an answer to arrive — and then writes down what it asked and what came back: no condition, no detail string, no count, no verdict exit code. The two predicates it keeps are named in its header: a poll's TERMINATION condition (built out of the plan's own data, and re-judged from the recorded series) and a HANDLE read out of an answer (`terminal_open`'s sid, a snapshot's `[ref=…]`) so the next call can be made at all. **AND THE GENERATED COPY HAS A PRODUCER NOW**: `index/public/summrise-agent/e2e.js` was a hand-`cp`'d copy that no gate compared to its source, and it is `summrise-e2e-judge --bundle`'s output, pinned by `agent/e2e-judge/tests/bundle.rs`
# ── AND THE SIX THE SWEEPS' AUDIT OF 2026-10-08 CLEARED, EACH BY READING ITS CONTROL FLOW RATHER THAN ITS NAME ──
# The audit was run because the paragraph that used to claim "everything left is a boundary" was written without one,
# and it retracted two of its own findings (see the spec's §4.1). These six are the part that survived: none of them
# decides anything the judge or the plan does not already own, and each names the platform call it makes.
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep-bundle.mjs | the ASSEMBLER: it resolves each payload's requires and compiles what it returns, so a module that does not parse fails at the commit. A build step, and the emitter's own producer
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/contrast-probe.mjs | the in-page probe SOURCE — a template of code a browser evaluates to measure contrast. It ships as text into the page; the comparison against the requirement is what the payload still does in JS, and that is counted at the payload, not here
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/panel-render-audit.mjs | renders the harness HTML the sweep measures (and reads DECORATIVE_WAIVERS to label decorative rows in that fixture). It builds the surface under test
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/panel-stub.cjs | the STUB DEVICE: a fixture that answers the agent's API so the panel sweep can run with no device. Its thirty comparisons decide what the FAKE answers, which is test data rather than product behaviour
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/live-panel-probe.mjs | the EMITTER for the live-panel measurement: it writes a standalone program that runs ON THE DEVICE against 127.0.0.1:18080 and reads the panel token from the device's own config in-process. It is the same shape as `panel-render-audit.mjs` two rules above (an emitter whose product is a program a browser runs) and it is the carve-out AGENTS.md already carries in its own row — "the device calls it through `browser_run_script`, which takes a JS file, and the measurement runs in the DOM". **AND ITS VERDICT IS NOT ENFORCED BY ANY JOB**, which is written here rather than left to be guessed: it runs on a device, its numbers are read by a person, and the CI-runnable half of the same questions is what `panel-design-sweep.bash` measures on the harness. What it adds that no harness run can is the LIVE panel's own geometry — round 167 measured it at 1488 root nodes and 14 live sessions, where the harness has 366 and three — so it is kept for the differences a harness cannot show, not as a gate.
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/live-run.cjs | the live-panel program: it drives the panel the device is actually running and returns rows. One guard, no verdict
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/landing-run.cjs | a payload that drives a browser over one page and returns rows — measured: zero comparisons, and its two template literals are selectors
# ── AND THE TWO HOVER PAYLOADS LEFT LOGIC THE SAME DAY (2026-10-09) ──────────────────────────────────────────
# `LOGIC | agent/scripts/` covered them, and what it was counting was the CONTRAST VERDICT: `panel-run.cjs`
# compared each measured row against its requirement and built the sentence a reader reads, and
# `console-run.cjs` did it TWICE with two different rules. Both now hand over every row the probe measured
# and `sweep-judge/src/hover.rs` (and its twin in `summrise-command-core`) applies the rule and formats the
# line, so nothing here decides anything: the loop measures, deduplicates identical rows by identity — which
# is a size guard with no verdict in it — and names the pass it measured, because the console's dark pass is
# not its light one. **THE NUMBER THAT LOOKED LIKE THE PRICE OF THIS WAS WRONG, AND MEASURING IT IS WHAT
# SETTLED IT**: the 2026-10-09 oracle run reported 218 samples for 19 lines, which reads like a report that
# would explode without a filter in the payload — but those are the SAME rows re-measured once per hovered
# control, and the identity dedup already collapses them. Measured on that report: an unfiltered entry
# carries 41 rows rather than 20, and all four cost +27 KB of a 430 KB report. **LOGIC 107 -> 105.**
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/panel-run.cjs | the PANEL payload: it drives the browser, evaluates the probes and returns the raw rows the judge decides on. It compares nothing — the contrast rule and its sentence moved to `sweep-judge/src/hover.rs` (2026-10-09) — and what is left it does not interpret: `rule` is the name of the pass it measured, and the identity dedup is a size guard
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/lib/sweep/console-run.cjs | the CONSOLE payload, the same shape, with one thing the panel's has not: THREE hover sites that were NOT one rule written three times — the dark pass skips graphics and has no 4.5 default, the light pass is the panel's comparison with a shorter sentence — so the entry names which one it measured. The rules and the sentences are the judge's
BOUNDARY | .agents/skills/setup-ts-deep-modules/ | a tooling config for the skill, not product code
BOUNDARY | docs/superpowers/p0/ | the P0 measurement harness — historical evidence, and a deletion candidate
BOUNDARY | proxies/api-relay/relay/ | the relay crate's own harness
BOUNDARY | proxies/summrise-relay/ | the retired relay worker's harness, kept for the differential

# ── LOGIC: the work that is left ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BOUNDARY | agent/scripts/ | **THE DESIGN SWEEPS' DRIVER AND JUDGE ARE RUST AND THIS DIRECTORY IS WHAT DECIDES NOTHING**
# (landing 2, 2026-10-10). The rule stood as LOGIC for the whole migration and it was the last one under this
# directory; every file it covered had already been given a longer, more specific BOUNDARY rule above — so it was
# SHADOWED and matched no file, while a reader consulting the manifest was told that a directory of boundaries is
# work that is left. What is left here is exactly the two things a JS file is for: the page-side PROBES, which a
# browser evaluates because `browser_run_script` takes a JS file, and the DEVICE-SIDE RUN PROGRAMS (`lib/sweep/*.cjs`),
# which perform the platform calls. Every decision they consult is Rust — `summrise-sweep-plan` for which surfaces and
# which passes, `summrise-sweep-judge` for the rules and the ladder and the budgets, `summrise-design-sweep-driver`
# for the step list and the probe assembly. **AND THE COUNT DID NOT MOVE, WHICH IS THE HONEST PART**: this
# reclassification is worth doing because the manifest is the answer to "may I write this in JS" and a LOGIC rule
# over a directory of boundaries answers it wrongly — not because a number fell. `MAX_LOGIC` is measured on the tree
# that carries the change and it is unchanged at 91, in two rules, both under `gateway/`.
BOUNDARY | scripts/test/lib/emitted-pieces.mjs | a FIXTURE READER, not a decision: it reads the PIECES module out of an emitter's artifact and hands it back as data. Two live bash gates import it — `panel-design-sweep.bash:92` and `sweep-judges.bash:134` — so it belongs to THEIR tooling the way the sweeps' in-page probes belong to theirs: it spawns no toolchain, computes no verdict, and a gate goes red if it stops reading. NOTE WHERE ITS SIBLING WENT: `scripts/test/lib/decomment.mjs` is DELETED in this commit, because the rule it defines now has exactly one definition and it is in Rust (`agent/tests/common/mod.rs`'s `decomment`/`decomment_line`/`decommented_corpus`, whose header says it took the rule FROM that file). Measured before deleting, as this repository requires: `git grep -nE '(from|import|require).*decomment' -- '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.js'` returned ONE line — a comment in its sibling naming it.
# **BOTH RULES THIS BLOCK HELD ARE DELETED, AND EACH SIDE OF THE MERGE DELETED ONE OF THEM.** They were
# the last two LOGIC rules outside `agent/scripts/`, they matched ONE file each, and both files left on
# 2026-10-09/10: `npm-test-floored.mjs` (this branch) and `packaging.test.mjs` (main). Neither rule is
# left matching nothing, and no file is orphaned by their removal — `scripts/test/lib/emitted-pieces.mjs`
# is a JS file still under `scripts/test/`, and it is covered by its own BOUNDARY rule above, which is a
# longer pattern than the directory rule that used to stand here.
# `scripts/test/` HAS NO JAVASCRIPT IN IT ANY MORE. The rule that stood here was `LOGIC | scripts/test/ |`
# and it existed for ONE file, `npm-test-floored.mjs` — the last one — whose DECISION had already moved
# (`agent/tests/npm_test_floor.rs`, landing 3) while its spawn had not. The spawn is in that same Rust file
# now: it derives every tracked package that declares a `test` script (`git ls-files`, so a `node_modules`
# copy cannot answer) and floors the ones whose RUNNER needs it — `node --test`, which prints `ℹ pass 0` and
# exits 0, where `vitest` refuses an empty suite itself (measured: `No test files found, exiting with code
# 1`). The rule is DELETED rather than left matching nothing — the same shape the `scripts/` rule got when
# `model-drift.mjs` became a crate. NOTE WHAT THE DERIVATION FOUND THAT THE LIST DID NOT:
# `agent/summrise-workspace-dsh` declares a suite and NO CI step ran it.
# `agent/summrise-agent-npm/` HAS NO JAVASCRIPT AT ALL NOW, and the last file left for the reason the class
# exists: `test/packaging.test.mjs` held ten cases and every one was a VALIDATION, so it was LOGIC and it had to
# become Rust. It is `agent/tests/npm_package.rs` (11 cases) — the SPAWN stayed a boundary (`npm pack --dry-run
# --json` decides the entry list, and it is asked to PACK, never to judge) and the checks are Rust, which is also
# what let the port ADD a link the `.mjs` could not: the entry list npm would write is now held against
# `required-in-tgz.txt`, where the JavaScript only ever compared the two committed LISTS to each other. The CLI's
# own decisions left this package earlier in the same landing (agent/summrise-cli), and the corpus that TypeScript
# left behind pins them answer-by-answer (`agent/summrise-cli/parity/expected.json`, 162 cases).

# ── AND THE ELECTRON SHELL LEFT THE LIST IN LANDING 6b, WHICH IS WHY ITS REASON IS LONGER THAN THE OTHERS ──
# Landing 6a moved the URL/origin/certificate policy out of this directory and this rule's reason said the
# remaining decisions were "token/auth, the loopback control server, agent lifecycle, window policy".
# **THAT REASON WAS TRUE AND INCOMPLETE**: the classification made before landing 6b's port found ~58
# decision sites and FOUR GROUPS THE REASON DID NOT NAME — the native MENU table (every label, accelerator
# and command id), the SCHTASKS argv and the auto-launch plan, the `/api/status` parse plus the two
# tray formatters, and the harness-door parse. A reason that is merely believed is how the next reader
# re-derives the gap, so the four are named here and the crate's own module headers carry them.
#
# WHAT IS LEFT IS NOTHING THIS CLASS COVERS. `main.ts` is now the native host: it creates windows, owns
# the tray, wires `ipcMain`, opens CDP :9333, spawns `schtasks`, reads `config.yaml` and makes HTTP
# requests — platform calls that decide nothing, because every question they ask is answered by
# `agent/summrise-shell-policy` (wasm) or `agent/summrise-url-policy` (wasm). The one document still
# written here is the wait page, and it is a template with its own inline script: a RENDERER program, not
# a decision this file makes. `preload.ts` was ALREADY pure boundary — four `contextBridge.exposeInWorld`
# calls, straight pass-through to `ipcRenderer`, literal channel names, no branch — and it must stay
# dependency-free, because the main window runs `sandbox: true`.
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/src/ | the Electron shell's HOST: windows, tray, IPC wiring, the :9333 switch, schtasks spawns, config reads and HTTP requests — platform calls, and every decision they ask about moved to `agent/summrise-shell-policy` (landing 6b) or `agent/summrise-url-policy` (landing 6a). NAMED, because "every decision" is what the previous reason said and it named none of the four groups a reader would not guess: the native MENU TABLE (`menu.rs`), the SCHTASKS argv and the auto-launch create-if-absent / end-and-delete plan (`lifecycle.rs`), the `/api/status` parse and the tray's uptime and clock formatters (`tray.rs`), and the HARNESS-DOOR parse of `answer.harnesses[].local_port` (`lifecycle.rs`, `sessions.rs`) — with the token regex, the port precedence, the loopback control server's route table and CORS decision, the AUMID and the window and slot policy (`sessions.rs`, `boot.rs`) beside them. The one document written here is the wait page, a template plus its own inline script. `preload.ts` must stay dependency-free: the main window runs `sandbox: true`, so requiring wasm there is a risk the design does not need
# THE SHELL'S TWO REMAINING TESTS ARE BOUNDARY FOR THE MANIFEST'S OWN REASON — "a test belongs to the code
# it tests". What they test is the HOST: `ipc-door.test.mjs` counts CALL SITES in `main.ts`'s own text
# (`ipcMain.handle` exactly once, `sanitizeBrowserUrl` exactly once, `loadTarget` used at least four
# times, the preload's channels equal the door's), and `embedded-bridge.test.mjs` pins the preload's
# exposed member names against the panel's fixture. Both are properties of an Electron boundary that can
# only be checked by reading the two files, and neither computes anything. THE ONE ASSERTION THAT WAS A
# DECISION — the shape of the forbidden-frame refusal, `{ok: false, error: "forbidden frame"}`, which the
# SPA reads — moved to `agent/summrise-shell-policy/src/tests.rs` in landing 6b, and what the `.mjs` case
# keeps is the count: the refusal is built once, from the policy, and the literal is not restated here.
BOUNDARY | agent/summrise-desktop-electron/test/ | the two tests of the HOST's own wiring — call-site counts in main.ts and the preload's bridge names. The decision tests that used to live here are `agent/summrise-shell-policy`'s
BOUNDARY | gateway/src/store.ts | **A PURE RE-EXPORT SHIM — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-12).** Its entire
#   non-comment body is nine `export * from "./store/<domain>.ts"` lines and nothing else: no condition, no default,
#   no table. It decides NOTHING; the implementation is `src/store/<domain>.ts`, which this rule keeps as LOGIC. A
#   barrel is structure, and structure is not a decision — the same reading "a fixture is not a decision" already
#   applies one file over.
LOGIC | gateway/src/ | the console worker's entry and plugins — A6 (landing 5)
LOGIC | gateway/test/ | the console worker's suite (landing 5)
BOUNDARY | gateway/config/ | **A DOCUMENT, NOT A DECISION — AND ITS TYPE IS COMPILER-CHECKED.** `models.ts` exports `{ providers: [], models: [], overrides: [] } satisfies CatalogueFile` — three EMPTY arrays, so it decides nothing today. It is `.ts` rather than `.json` for a measured reason its own header gives: a JSON import needs `with { type: "json" }` in Node and different syntax in the bundler, so a document the TESTS import would not be the same document the WORKER imports — while `satisfies` makes `tsc` refuse a misspelled `contextWindows` or an effort the router cannot speak BEFORE anything parses it at runtime. The DECISIONS this document feeds (file-over-KV precedence, what may be declared, the routing fields refused by name) live in `gateway/src/store/file-config.ts`, which is LOGIC with the rest of the console's rollback.
# ── THE INDEX'S JAVASCRIPT IS THE ORACLE, NOT WORK THAT IS LEFT (measured 2026-10-09) ─────────────────────────
# The index worker was cut over to Rust before this migration began, and these files were still counted as
# LOGIC on the assumption that their cutover was simply unharvested. Reading what depends on them says
# otherwise, and each dependency is named here because "delete the old implementation" was the wrong move:
#   * `index/worker/verify.mjs` drives `index/src/index.js` AS PUBLISHED, with stub bindings, and diffs status,
#     sorted headers and body bytes against the Rust — it is the differential, and deleting it deletes the proof.
#   * `agent/scripts/landing-design-sweep.mjs` does `import { PAGE } from "../../index/src/page.js"` — a LIVE
#     import by a tool that renders the page under test.
#   * `index/landing/verify.mjs` reads `page.js` out of a pinned commit with `git show <ref>:…`, so that file's
#     history is the reference the landing page is measured against.
# The Rust is what runs (`index/wrangler.jsonc` names `worker/build/index.js`, measured by fetching the deployed
# module from the API and finding the wasm glue in it), so nothing here decides product behaviour: these files
# exist to be COMPARED WITH, which is the boundary `agent/summrise-cli/parity/` and the sweeps' parity
# instrument are already classified as.
BOUNDARY | index/src/ | the ORACLE the Rust index worker is measured against (`verify.mjs` drives this entry with stub bindings; the landing sweep imports `PAGE` from `page.js`). The Rust is what runs
BOUNDARY | index/test/ | the oracle's own suite: it exercises the JavaScript the differential drives, and it leaves when the differential does — not when the worker does
BOUNDARY | proxies/api-relay/api/ | **THE RELAY'S ORACLE, NOT ITS LOGIC — AND CI SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS.** ci.yml calls this suite "the ORACLE the committed fixture was generated from" (73 cases, its own `node --test` step), and three Rust gates read these files as TEXT: `agent/tests/proxy_timeout_parity.rs` and `proxy_cors_parity.rs` compare the Rust's timeout/header and CORS constants against `git.ts`/`github.ts`/`gform.ts`/`zen.js`/`proxy.js`, and `relay/tests/two_relays_agree.rs` reads `git.ts`/`github.ts` for the hosts and env-var names. `relay/differential.mjs` compares the two implementations' byte-for-byte answers on 14 requests, and that comparison needs both sides present. **The Rust relay is what serves**: nginx's `/api/` was pointed at `127.0.0.1:8082` on 2026-10-09 and proved by stopping the Node unit (the public endpoint still answered 401 with only the Rust one up). The Node bundle stays deployed as the one-line rollback, which is the second reason its source cannot leave. Deleting these files would delete the proof and the fallback, not the work — the work moved to `proxies/api-relay/relay/`, which the manifest already carries as BOUNDARY.
BOUNDARY | proxies/api-relay/server/ | the same oracle half, one layer up: `routing.mjs` is the pure URL routing + entry plumbing whose decisions moved to Rust first (`relay/src/`, covered by `cargo test --manifest-path proxies/api-relay/relay/Cargo.toml` in CI), and `entry.mjs` is what `build-relay.sh` stages into `dist/entry.mjs` for the differential and for the deployed rollback bundle. Its own suite (`server/test/`) is the oracle's proof, for the reason the paragraph above gives.
# ── AND THE ROOT `scripts/` RULE IS GONE, BECAUSE ITS ONLY MATCH IS (2026-10-09) ─────────────────────────────
# `LOGIC | scripts/ | the root build/release tooling (landing 3)` was the catch-all for the root directory, and
# `scripts/model-drift.mjs` was its ONLY `.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`/`.ts` match: the rest of `scripts/` is extensionless
# hook scripts, which this inventory does not count, and `scripts/test/` is covered by its own longer rule. The
# file is `agent/model-drift/` now (crate `summrise-model-drift`), so the rule matched NOTHING — and a rule that
# matches nothing is dead weight in the file that answers "may I write this in JS". Deleting it is what makes a
# future `.mjs` in `scripts/` land as UNCLASSIFIED, which is the answer a reviewer wants.
